exposure: insertion of intrauterine contraception at cesarean section
intrauterine contraception (copper intrauterine device or levonorgestrel intrauterine system)
cohort: 877 women offered intrauterine contraception at elective cesarean section
finding: Routine provision of intrauterine contraception at elective cesarean section was feasible and acceptable, with good uptake and continuation rates for the first year.
mod_finding: The study found that routinely offering intrauterine contraception insertion during cesarean section is feasible, acceptable to women, and associated with good uptake and continuation rates.
